$comment: The voice-over: one take per scene. `text` is the line as WRITTEN ("17 weeks", "example.com"); the brand's pronunciation lexicon (brand-tokens.json brand.pronunciations) turns it into what the voice is sent, and the captions show the written forms. A take may instead give `speak`, sent exactly as written. Each take starts at `at` and must finish before `until`, in FILM seconds (after inserts). `scene` says what is on screen; `anchors` are words that should land while their picture shows (reported by npm run narrate, not enforced). `verify` sets the listening check (speech-to-text): the most word error a take may have and how many times to re-voice a take that fails. `timing` is 'tts' (the voice's own timestamps) or 'forced-alignment' (re-aligned against the text). The narrator comes from brand-tokens.json video.voice.narrator; `voice` here is only the fallback. `auditions` lists voices for npm run audition. Eleven v3/v4 reject a seed, so seed is null.

takes.scene: opening card: Brand films, made in code
takes.text: This film was made by a script, not an editor.

takes.scene: six weeks of edits stack up; the brand swatches drift
takes.text: Explainer videos take weeks of edits, and the brand drifts with every one.

takes.scene: render(t): a code card scrubs time and the picture follows
takes.text: brand-film writes the film as an HTML scene, where every frame is a function of time.

takes.scene: three takes: waveform, transcript, term chips checked
takes.text: ElevenLabs voices each line, then listens back to check every name was said right.

takes.scene: frame strip fills; 1,440 frames, -16 LUFS, captions
takes.text: Headless Chrome renders each frame, and ffmpeg mixes the voice, music and captions.

takes.scene: paper end card: Make the film in code; the GitHub URL
takes.text: Your brand, your story, made in code. Find brand-film on GitHub.
